note: Phase 1 drawing test (2026-10-02), revised the same day after John's review. Read by tools/contact_sheet.py. Credits and licences are in ../research/play-image-plan.json. The failed Iphigenia at Aulis test stays in rejected/ and off the sheet.

drawings.name: Aeschylus · the Pythia (Eumenides)
drawings.alt: The Pythia, Apollo's priestess, fleeing in terror with her hands raised
drawings.source: Bötticher's 1859 drawing of an Apulian krater, Orestes at Delphi (Heidelberg scan, public domain)
drawings.method: Engraved plate: cut along her own lines, with straight cuts across blank paper; Apollo's overlapping foot erased; potrace
drawings.verdict: Clean. Revised twice: arm, head curl, fingers, knee edge and the whole shawl are in. One line is drawn in: her dress's black stripe, continued 45px across the gap where Apollo's foot was erased.

drawings.name: Sophocles · Oedipus (before the Sphinx)
drawings.alt: Oedipus, a young traveller in cloak and short tunic, standing with a spear
drawings.source: Achilles Painter pelike, Berlin F 2355, photograph by Gary Todd (CC0)
drawings.method: Red-figure photo: clay found by colour (shiny glaze), fold lines by local contrast, hair outlined by hand, potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable. Revised: every cloak fold and the hat on his back now show. The painter's own drawing is sparer than the engravings; the lower cloak is ragged where the vase is restored.

drawings.name: Euripides · Iphigenia (Iphigenia in Tauris)
drawings.alt: Iphigenia, priestess of Artemis, holding out a letter tablet and the temple key
drawings.source: 1849 lithograph of the Buckingham vase, Archäologische Zeitung Taf. XII (public domain)
drawings.method: Lithograph: lines by local contrast, cut along her own lines, potrace
drawings.verdict: Clean. Revised twice: forearm, key hand, chain, sandals, veil edge and the whole tablet are in. Pylades' fingertips on the tablet's far edge cannot be told apart at this scan's size.

drawings.name: Aristophanes · Mika (Women at the Thesmophoria)
drawings.alt: Mika, in a comic old woman's mask, holding out a bowl
drawings.source: Würzburg krater H 5697, photograph by ArchaiOptix (CC BY-SA 4.0)
drawings.method: Red-figure photo: clay mask, fold lines by local contrast, Mnesilochus' knife cut away, potrace
drawings.verdict: Clean. Revised: the drapery folds now run their full length. The painter's own drawing is sparer than the engravings.

drawings.name: Medea · in the serpent chariot
drawings.alt: Medea in a chariot drawn by two serpents
drawings.source: Cleveland Museum of Art 1991.1, museum photograph, full-resolution TIFF (CC0)
drawings.method: Red-figure photo: clay mask, disk border cut away, netted sleeves kept; lines from the full-resolution TIFF; potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable. Revised twice: the face and the netted left sleeve now show, and in dark mode the goad and the gaps inside the figure carry the clay. Still the busiest drawing.

drawings.name: Oedipus Tyrannus · Oedipus at the messenger's news
drawings.alt: Oedipus, bearded, in a long embroidered robe, his hand at his beard, holding a staff
drawings.source: Sicilian calyx-krater, Syracuse, Museo Paolo Orsi 66557, photograph by Dan Diffendale (CC BY-NC-SA 2.0)
drawings.method: Red-figure photo: loose cut through the glaze, hand-drawn zones for floor, plaster, shoes and head; cracks erased and the lines they broke joined across them; lines broken by wear joined; staff redrawn as a straight rod; hair and beard drawn solid, face lines evened; hand redrawn after John's trace, every finger outlined; potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable. Revised after John's review: the hair and a fuller beard are solid, the face lines even, and the hand is redrawn after his trace with every finger outlined; the mended crack beside it is gone and lines broken by wear are joined. The hem and shoes are worn on the vase and stay rough.

drawings.name: Oedipus at Colonus · Oedipus at the altar between his daughters
drawings.alt: Blind Oedipus, white-haired and bearded, seated at an altar with his staff, one hand raised, between his daughters Ismene and Antigone
drawings.source: Apulian calyx-krater close to the De Schulthess Painter, formerly Melbourne, Geddes collection A 5:8; the photos in Green 2003 (pp. 4, 26, 29; HathiTrust mdp.39015060089391), with Ismene's lines and borders, and those of the altar's left end and the strip below p. 26, from a photo found online (source unknown), placed on their reprint in Taplin, Pots & Plays (2007) no. 27, checked against Digital LIMC photo 8569X101 (all in copyright)
drawings.method: Red-figure photos, Green's pages registered to the plate and laid over its 4x enlargement, Ismene's lines and borders (and those outside p. 26) from a photo found online: cut round the group and the altar, columns left out; one outline where a blur left a brown band; painted marks at their own widths, close ones along their centres, faint folds by a ridge filter, worn dashes joined; dark hair and Ismene's borders solid; Oedipus' face drawn on the paint of p. 29, the dark marks in his hair and beard solid, his staff in its two visible parts, his hand from the column's edge; the daughters' faces, and Antigone's hand and forearm, after John's traces; potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable; approved by John (2026-10-03). Oedipus redrawn from Green's p. 29 (his lower fingers from John's marks, the raised two turned a little apart so they read at display size); Antigone from John's traces on p. 26; Ismene's folds from the photo John found, her face from his traces and marks. Reviewed by Codex (GPT-6-Sol) and its fixes made. The zigzag ends of the two mantles are only as clear as the photos allow.
